native_mechanisms: A stone on a corner: a node's distance is finalized once settled and never reconsidered (permanent-label set).
A duck carries a spooled thread: each reached node holds a tentative label equal to the running sum of edge weights along the path to it (relaxation/tentative distance).
Each round, find the leader duck — the unstoned node with the shortest carried thread — and settle it before any further expansion (min-extraction over unsettled labels).
Discard threads that are not shorter than the far corner's current thread, and drop roads to already-stoned/dead-end houses unspooled (edge pruning on non-improvement).
Corners the ducks never reach stay bare — unreachable nodes keep infinite distance.
core_technique: Textbook Dijkstra on a CSR graph: O(n^2) linear array scan for the minimum tentative distance (a value-only vectorizable reduction plus an index-recovery pass) for small or dense graphs, switching to a standard binary-heap Dijkstra for large sparse graphs.
